segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: Okay, I think we're all here, let's get started. Thanks for making time, I know Friday afternoons are rough.

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: No worries, better than another Monday meeting.

segments.speaker: Tom Becker
segments.text: Agreed. So the agenda today is Q4 roadmap, and I want us to leave with a locked list, not a maybe list.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: Right. Quick recap of Q3 first. We shipped the new Alerting Engine, the Slack integration, and we finally closed out the CSV export bug that customers kept hitting.

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: And the onboarding flow redesign, don't forget that one.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: Yes, sorry, that too. Activation went up about eleven percent after that shipped.

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: Eleven percent, that's solid. Did that hold after the first two weeks or was it a novelty bump?

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: Held steady through August, so I think it's real.

segments.speaker: Tom Becker
segments.text: Good. Okay, Q4. The three big candidates on the table are Cohort Explorer version two, the Funnel Builder performance rework, and self serve billing. Anything I'm missing?

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: The dashboard redesign is technically Q4 too, but that's a separate design review, we don't need to relitigate it here.

segments.speaker: Tom Becker
segments.text: Right, that one's already scoped, Elena's team owns that.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: Let's start with Cohort Explorer v2 since that's the one sales keeps asking about.

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: What's actually changing in v2, functionally?

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: Three things. Saved cohort definitions so people stop rebuilding the same segment every week, cohort comparison side by side, and the ability to export a cohort straight into an email campaign tool.

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: The comparison view is the one customers ask about most in interviews, by a wide margin.

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: How big is that engineering lift? Comparison view sounds like it touches the query engine.

segments.speaker: Kenji Watanabe
segments.text: It does. Sorry, I know I'm not really on this call, Priya asked me to weigh in for ten minutes.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: Yeah, go ahead Kenji, you looked at the query side last week.

segments.speaker: Kenji Watanabe
segments.text: So comparison view means running two cohort queries in parallel and diffing them. Right now our query engine isn't built for that, it assumes one cohort at a time. I'd estimate three weeks just for the backend, plus caching work so it doesn't double our database load.

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: Three weeks for backend alone. Plus frontend, plus QA, that's basically five to six weeks total.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: That's roughly what I had penciled in too.

segments.speaker: Tom Becker
segments.text: And where does that leave the Funnel Builder rework?

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: That's the other big one. Funnel Builder queries are timing out for our larger customers, anyone above like two million events a month is seeing load times over ten seconds.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: Ten seconds, that's brutal, no wonder support tickets on this are up.

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: Support flagged eighteen tickets on funnel timeouts in the last thirty days. BrightLoop specifically has complained twice.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: BrightLoop again, they're one of our biggest accounts, Sarah's been managing that relationship pretty closely.

segments.speaker: Tom Becker
segments.text: How do we fix it, and how long?

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: We need to precompute funnel steps instead of running them live every time. That's a materialized view approach. I'd say four weeks, and Kenji would be the one building most of it.

segments.speaker: Kenji Watanabe
segments.text: Four weeks is optimistic if we also want backfill for existing funnels, not just new ones going forward. I'd say five to be safe.

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: Fair, let's say five.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: Okay so if we do Cohort Explorer v2 at six weeks and Funnel Builder at five weeks, that's basically our whole quarter for two backend engineers.

segments.speaker: Tom Becker
segments.text: Which means self serve billing doesn't happen this quarter, realistically.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: I think that's the right call honestly, billing was always going to be more of a growth bet, and the funnel timeouts are actively costing us renewals.

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: Can I push back slightly? What if we do a scoped version of Funnel Builder first, just fix the timeout for the top twenty accounts by usage, and defer the full backfill to Q1?

segments.speaker: Kenji Watanabe
segments.text: That's actually doable in about two and a half weeks if we just target the accounts over the two million event threshold.

segments.speaker: Tom Becker
segments.text: I like that. That frees up time for at least a slice of billing work.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: Okay, let's do that. Funnel Builder scoped fix first, two and a half weeks, then Cohort Explorer v2, then whatever's left goes to billing groundwork, not a full launch.

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: For Cohort Explorer v2, I'll need final requirements from Priya by end of next week if we want mockups ready in time for the engineering kickoff.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: That works, I'll get you a written spec by Wednesday so you have a couple extra days.

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: Perfect, I can turn mockups around in about a week after that.

segments.speaker: Tom Becker
segments.text: Let's talk pricing tiers for a second, since that connects to billing anyway.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: Right, so the proposal is we introduce a Growth tier between Starter and Enterprise, priced around four hundred and ninety dollars a month, that unlocks Cohort Explorer and the Alerting Engine.

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: Is four ninety based on anything or is that a guess?

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: It's based on the willingness to pay survey we ran in July, most respondents in that segment said they'd pay between four fifty and five fifty for those two features combined.

segments.speaker: Tom Becker
segments.text: What about existing Starter customers who already have Cohort Explorer through a grandfathered plan?

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: Good question, I think we grandfather anyone who signed before the tier launches, otherwise we'll get a wave of angry emails.

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: Agreed, nothing kills trust faster than taking away a feature someone's paying for.

segments.speaker: Tom Becker
segments.text: Okay, write that up as a formal doc, I want legal and finance to see it before we announce anything.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: I'll have a draft doc ready by next Monday.

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: Switching gears, can we talk headcount? I've had an open backend req for six weeks now and it's slowing everything down.

segments.speaker: Tom Becker
segments.text: I know, I approved the budget line two weeks ago, it's stuck in an approval queue on my end, that's on me.

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: If we're doing Cohort Explorer and Funnel Builder in the same quarter with the same two engineers, someone's going to burn out, probably Kenji.

segments.speaker: Kenji Watanabe
segments.text: I appreciate you saying that out loud.

segments.speaker: Tom Becker
segments.text: Noted. I'll get the req formally approved by end of day Monday, no more sitting in queue.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: Thank you. Okay, let's also touch on risks quickly. What could blow up this plan?

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: Biggest risk is the materialized view work for Funnel Builder touching the same database tables that the alerting engine reads from. If we're not careful we could introduce alerting delays.

segments.speaker: Kenji Watanabe
segments.text: I'll write a short design doc before I start so we catch that early, should take me a day.

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: From design side, the risk is scope creep on comparison view, stakeholders always want one more filter option once they see the mockup.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: I'll own keeping that scoped, we can put extra filters in a v2.1 backlog.

segments.speaker: Tom Becker
segments.text: One more risk I want to name, competitively. Have we heard anything about what our competitors are doing on funnel analytics specifically? I don't want us to be reactive instead of ahead of the market.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: From what I've seen in win loss notes, our two main competitors, Metricly and Pathframe, both still lack real time funnel updates, everything they have is batch, refreshed once a day at best.

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: That's actually a meaningful gap we could lean into once the materialized view work is done, since ours will effectively refresh much faster.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: I'll talk to marketing about positioning around performance once we have the before and after numbers Marcus mentioned earlier, once we've validated them.

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: One more small thing on risk, we haven't talked about the Query Composer team's roadmap. Are they planning any changes that could conflict with either of our two big Q4 items?

segments.speaker: Kenji Watanabe
segments.text: I checked with them last week actually, they have a change planned in October to how filters get parsed internally, which could touch the same code path as Cohort Explorer's comparison view. I'll set up time with their lead this week to compare timelines.

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: Appreciate you catching that, that kind of cross team collision is exactly the sort of thing that blows up a quarter if it's missed.

segments.speaker: Tom Becker
segments.text: Good. Anything else before we wrap?

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: Just a reminder that our on call rotation changes next week, Dimitri's taking over from me.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: Noted, unrelated to roadmap but good to know.

segments.speaker: Tom Becker
segments.text: Alright. Let's recap decisions. Funnel Builder scoped fix first, roughly two and a half weeks. Cohort Explorer v2 next, roughly five to six weeks including comparison view. Billing gets whatever's left as groundwork only, not a launch. Pricing doc goes to legal and finance next week.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: And Elena gets the written spec by Wednesday, mockups about a week after.

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: And I'll get you the funnel timeout numbers, actual latency figures, by Wednesday too so we have a baseline to compare against once the fix ships.

segments.speaker: Tom Becker
segments.text: Great, and I'll push the headcount approval through by Monday.

segments.speaker: Priya Sharma
segments.text: Sounds like a plan. Thanks everyone, same time next month for the Q4 check in.

segments.speaker: Elena Vasquez
segments.text: Sounds good, talk soon.

segments.speaker: Kenji Watanabe
segments.text: Thanks, bye.

segments.speaker: Marcus Johnson
segments.text: Later.

summary.overview:
The team locked in the Q4 roadmap for Acme Pulse, prioritizing a scoped fix for Funnel Builder query timeouts (affecting accounts above two million monthly events, including BrightLoop Retail) ahead of a fuller backfill planned for Q1. Cohort Explorer v2, including a new side-by-side cohort comparison view, was approved as the second major initiative, with Elena delivering mockups roughly a week after Priya circulates a written spec. Self serve billing was deprioritized to groundwork only given limited backend capacity.

The team also discussed introducing a new Growth pricing tier at approximately $490/month bundling Cohort Explorer and the Alerting Engine, based on July's willingness-to-pay survey, with existing Starter customers to be grandfathered. Tom committed to pushing through a long-stalled backend headcount approval by Monday to reduce load on Kenji and Marcus.

Open questions include finalizing the pricing doc with legal and finance, and guarding against scope creep on the cohort comparison view once stakeholders see the mockups. The team also noted a competitive opening around real time funnel refresh versus batch-only competitors like Metricly and Pathframe, and flagged a possible collision with the Query Composer team's planned October filter parsing changes that Kenji will sync on directly.

Deliver Cohort Explorer v2 mockups about a week after receiving the written spec

Draft the Growth pricing tier doc for legal and finance review
Push through the approval for the open backend engineer requisition by Monday
